title: Normal-state self-consistent solution (δ=0.20)
action: Implement the two-pole approximation self-consistent equations for the normal state of the extended Hubbard model with parameters t=-1.0 eV, t2=0.3|t|, U=-8t, and doping δ=0.20. Solve iteratively for the chemical potential μ, correlation functions (n_{ijσ}, m_{ijσ}, spin-spin correlations), band shift W_{kσ}, and the quasiparticle energies ω₁(k), ω₂(k) and spectral function A(k,ω).
description: Required intermediate to obtain the normal-state scored artifacts; the self-consistent loop converges correlation functions and band renormalizations.

title: Normal spectral function A(k,ω=0)
action: From the converged normal-state solution, compute the spectral function A(k,ω=0) on a uniform grid of k-points covering the first Brillouin zone. Save the data.
description: Fermi surface spectral weight at ω=0 for doping δ=0.20; used to verify the presence of a hole pocket around (π/2,π/2) and a pseudogap near (0,π).

title: Quasiparticle band energies
action: From the converged normal-state solution, extract the two quasiparticle band energies ω₁ and ω₂ along the high-symmetry path Γ–X–M–Γ. Save the data.
description: Quasiparticle band dispersions for doping δ=0.20; used to verify band crossing near (π/2,π/2) and a gap near (0,π).
output_schema: columns: kx (float, 1/Å), ky (float, 1/Å), omega1 (float, eV), omega2 (float, eV)

title: Superconducting self-consistent gap calculation for n_T=0.90
action: Implement the two-pole approximation equations for the superconducting state of the Hubbard model with n_T=0.90, U=-8t, t=-1.0 eV, t2=0.3|t|. Using a normal-state solution at that filling as initial guess, solve the d-wave gap equation self-consistently for a series of temperatures from near zero to above the critical temperature T_c. Record the converged gap amplitude Δ at each temperature.
description: Required intermediate to obtain the superconducting gap scored artifact; the loop solves the gap equation and updates correlation functions iteratively at each temperature.

title: Superconducting gap Δ(T)
action: From the temperature series of converged gap amplitudes, extract the gap Δ as a function of temperature. Save the Δ(T) data.
description: d-wave superconducting gap amplitude vs temperature for n_T=0.90 and U=-8t; used to extract zero-temperature gap Δ₀, critical temperature T_c, and the low-temperature upturn Δ_max−Δ₀.
output_schema: columns: T (float, reduced temperature k_B T/|t|, dimensionless), Delta (float, gap amplitude in eV)
